title: Co-borrower liability disputes - the common misconceptions
p1:
Think a co-borrower can simply walk away from a loan because they did not use the money? That belief can create serious financial surprises.

Many people assume being a co-borrower is just a supporting role. The reality is often very different.
p2:
A common misconception is that only the person who spends the loan amount is responsible for repayment. In many cases, a co-borrower has a legal responsibility to repay the loan if the primary borrower fails to do so.

The bank usually looks at the loan agreement, not who actually enjoyed the funds.
p3:
This means a co-borrower may face repayment demands, credit score impact, and legal consequences even if they were not the person making purchases or using the money.

Before signing as a co-borrower, understand the terms, repayment obligations, and risks involved. A signature on a loan document can create a responsibility that lasts much longer than expected.
